coordinate_policy: reuse the exact minimum-L1 Eisenstein lattice representative; recover x=a+b and y=-b so k=x+y*omega modulo the subgroup order
digit_policy: balanced radix 256, remainders in [-128,127], least significant window first; use a checked generic fallback if either coordinate exceeds the prepared positions
endomorphism_policy: use omega(P)=(beta*x,y) for the second coordinate; reuse the identical positive-magnitude table for both coordinates and negate the point for negative digits
online_policy: sum all nonzero signed window points in one Jacobian accumulator, then convert one output to affine; public scalars only
preparation_policy: for every position i prepare [d*256^i]P for d=1..128, normalize all points with one batch inversion
training_observation: mean nonzero signed digits were 3.88 on glv-j0-32 and 7.84 on j0-56; maximum observed window positions were 2 and 4; no CPU speedup inferred
